messages:
monica: quick follow-up from the RFC — proposing we incrementally prune the telemetry ingest pipeline: move heavy enrichers to a dedicated sidecar and collapse duplicate transforms. goal: pay down tech debt and cut egress/cpu cost without risking hotpath latency. want alignment on ordering and rollback plan.
sam: +1 to sidecarization, but worried about lifecycle complexity for tenants that still rely on old transforms. do we keep a compatibility shim? :thinking:
rafael: we should sequence by traffic: start with low-traffic cohorts and a single vendor integration. that gives us real metrics before moving core tenants.
dina: suggestion: three-phase approach — 1) sidecar for non-critical enrichers, 2) backfill + compare outputs for parity, 3) cutover + deprecation window. provides audit trail.
anya: add canary routing and a golden set of prompts to validate semantic parity. curious about cost math: what's the expected CPU reduction?
monica: rough estimate: 18-25% CPU reduction on ingest path for typical batch sizes based on the profiler. egress savings depend on whether we dedupe before emit. we'll publish numbers after the spike test.
rafael: rollback safety: keep the old transformer around for 2 weeks and route 5-10% of traffic to it after cutover. if drift > 0.5% on key metrics -> flip.
dina: agree. also add a feature flag gate per-tenant so we can opt-out quickly.
monica: ops checklist draft: ```- deploy sidecar image v1 (feature-flag disabled)
- run backfill compare job (50k events)
- enable canary (5% traffic) for cohort A
- monitor ingest-latency, enrich-coverage, cost delta
- ramp to 100% for A, then B, then global
- deprecate old transformer after 14d```
anya: one gotcha: observability tagging will change — we need to ensure traces and logs remain linkable (trace id propagation). otherwise incident blames become hard.
monica: good call. we'll include trace-id header pass-through and add a migration test in the pipeline.
infra-bot: deploy pipeline note: "telemetry-sidecar-v1" staged to dev at 2025-06-12T16:02Z. CI integration for backfill job added.
sam: long-term question: do we standardize sidecar contract (proto/http) or allow heterogenous adapters? standard contract reduces coupling later.
rafael: standardize. define a minimal JSON contract and support a tiny adapter shim for any legacy behavior. keeps runtime simple.
dina: and document cost/accountability lines — which team owns sidecar SLAs and compensating resources. don't assume platform will absorb the extra infra.
monica: noted — will add ownership to the rollout doc. also adding a tech-debt play: post-cutover, schedule a 2-sprint cleanup to remove dead code paths.
anya: small request: include a regression evaluation step against our sample prompts (embedding drift & token diff). we can add a regression job to the eval-engine.
monica: done. i'll update the RFC with the phase gates and attach the checklist. can folks react with :thumbsup: if they approve sequence?
sam: :thumbsup:
rafael: :thumbsup:
dina: :thumbsup:
anya: :thumbsup:
monica: thanks — I'll create the rollout epic and tag ownership. if anything else, reply here and I'll fold it in.
